references.text: Continuation of the theophany at Sinai, where smoke rises because the Lord descends in fire
The people experience thunder, lightning, the sound of the shofar, and the smoking mountain, and they tremble with fear
Moses reminds the people that the mountain burned with fire up to heaven, with darkness, clouds, and fog
Moses recounts the event at Sinai with the fire, cloud, and darkness, and the people's fear
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to the Sinai event with fire, darkness, storm, and trumpet sound
Lightning, rumblings, and thunder proceed from the throne, reminiscent of the theophany at Sinai
Thunder, rumblings, lightning, and earthquakes as signs of God's presence, like the Sinai event
Lightning, rumblings, thunder, earthquakes, and hail at the revelation of the ark of the covenant
Describes God's coming with a thunderstorm, lightning, dark clouds, and trumpet sound as signs of his power
Refers to God's thunder, lightning, and earthquakes at the deliverance from Egypt
Clouds, darkness, fire, and lightning surround the Lord when he reveals himself
A prophetic allusion using the Sinai event as an image of the day of the Lord.
